about: Groddle Afternoon build notes. One object per post, newest first. Text fields are HTML fragments. Posts with "archived" were lifted word for word from the old build archive by tools/changelog/extract.mjs; "draft": true builds the page but leaves it out of the list. archive.title: Groddle Field Notes · Build archive
archive.heading: Many long nights in Ur.
archive.lead: From the first recovered street to returning quests, untangled trees, restored rocks, and an interface that learned some manners.

posts.label: VECTOR PARTS
posts.title: Every Glitch got sharp, and the Butler learned to say hi
posts.summary: Avatars are drawn from Tiny Speck’s own vector parts, your Butler can be rebuilt piece by piece, and the Hall of Rejected Concepts is open again.
posts.eyebrow: VECTOR AVATARS · THE BUTLER · REJECTED CONCEPTS · PLAYERS’ SNAPS · ANIMALS
posts.subtitle: Drawn from the pieces Tiny Speck left behind.
posts.lead: Every Glitch in the game is now drawn from Tiny Speck’s vector parts, and the old bitmap avatars are gone: they were real players’ avatars caught by the Wayback Machine, so they were only ever reference. New players start from the original avatar picker, with four choices for each of nine parts, and the presets gained four Starter looks and thirteen Costumes. Your Butler can be rebuilt part by part from its own Flash doll and trades hi signs with you each day. Behind the Mezzanine, the Hall of Rejected Concepts is open again, and a few rooms that never made it into the archive now look the way players’ Snaps show them.

stat.caption: exhibits back in the Hall of Rejected Concepts, each with the caption its button raised

image.alt: The default Glitch in a brown bowler hat.
image.caption: The default Glitch, drawn from Tiny Speck’s vector parts.

cards.title: Every Glitch drawn sharp
cards.text: You, the rivals, guests and companions are all drawn from Tiny Speck’s vector parts now, and old saves move to the nearest vector look. Start fresh opens the original new-player picker: nine parts, four choices each. Four Starter looks and thirteen Costumes join the presets, so you can dress as the Rook, a giant, a chicken or a garden gnome.

cards.title: A Butler of your own making
cards.text: The Butler’s Flash doll was flattened into 171 parts, so you can change its head, face, accessory, body, arms and legs one at a time, or randomize the lot. Press 5 to flash your hi sign for the day: the Butler says hi back once a day, with a bonus when your signs match.

cards.title: The Hall of Rejected Concepts
cards.text: Behind the Mezzanine, fourteen exhibits stand in their recorded order, from the Rube to Avatars. The room is laid out from ten players’ Snaps and two recordings, and each Wall Button raises Tiny Speck’s own caption for its exhibit, like “A bunny. Why? Because bunny.”

cards.title: Rooms as players saw them
cards.text: Mr. Block’s playroom is the giant Kid’s Room again, with monster wallpaper, a bed, a panda and a tea party. The Rube’s yard is a dusky junk garden of flamingos, lanterns and a rook skull, and Operation Grow’s stalks turn teal and glow as they bloom. None of the three survived in the archive, so they are dressed from players’ Snaps.

cards.title: Sky Plunge lands softly
cards.text: The only picture of the course, a player’s Snap from October 2012, sets the landing: a cream-gold sky, sun rays and a white cloud floor, with a Back to Top door and “AHHHHH YEAHHHH!!!!!” in the clouds. A Qurazy quoin hides on the way down.

cards.title: Crowded streets
cards.text: Pack too many animals onto one street and they sulk, grumble and sometimes leave, and at the limit one puffs away. Hechey Track holds 20 piggies and a starter yard 18; the Happy Animals cards raise your yard to 20, then 22.

cards.title: Shake the Elemental Pouch
cards.text: Buy one from a hardware, alchemical, tool or mining vendor, which also completes Get Elemental!, and shake it once a game day for bonus elements.

cards.title: Lanterns, loading cards and chatty plots
cards.text: Jack-O-Lanterns are drawn sharp from their Flash files, all 74 frames in the original order. The loading card remembers when you were last on a street and what lives there, and garden plots answer every plant, water, hoe and pick with lines from all 31 of the original talkback pools.

posts.label: THE WHOLE WORLD
posts.title: Ur got its depth, its names, its kitchens, and its afterlife
posts.summary: Every street now scrolls in true parallax under its own sky, the Magic Rock hands out real quests, and croaking sends you to Naraka.
posts.eyebrow: PARALLAX · 285 RECIPES · NARAKA · MAGIC ROCK QUESTS · PUBLIC STREET NAMES
posts.subtitle: From a scrap of Ur toward all of it.
posts.lead: The first street import had quietly dropped each layer's size, colour treatment, and sky. Restoring them from the archived location XML turned flat backdrops into deep, blurred forests and Naraka's red sky with black silhouettes, using a port of the client's own colour matrix. Mirrored decorations face the right way again, and 573 streets now carry the names players actually saw. The making panel grew from 41 to 285 source recipes across 28 tools, every street spirit sells its real stock, croaking at zero energy sends you to Hell One to squish eleven bunches of grapes, and the Magic Rock now offers the original quests with their original dialogue.

stat.caption: street layers whose original colour treatment returned

cards.title: True parallax and skies
cards.text: Background and foreground canvases slide with the client's parallax rule, 1,226 streets get their own gradient sky, and blurred layers bake once at half resolution.

cards.title: Croak and come back
cards.text: Zero energy sends you to Hell One. Squish eleven bunches of Hellish Grapes to return at ten percent energy; the dead walk greyscale, like the original.

cards.title: The Magic Rock's quests
cards.text: One quest offer at a time, with the original conversations. Accepted quests advance from crafting, vendors, mail, harvests, verbs, visits, and your pack.

cards.title: A full kitchen
cards.text: Saucepans, the Famous Pugilist Grill, cocktail shakers, the Awesome Pot, seasoners, and the cauldron, with source energy and mood for 193 foods and 26 drinks.

cards.title: Every street spirit
cards.text: Fifteen stores at source prices, and 893 streets now host the vendor the production map assigned them.

cards.title: A world to harvest
cards.text: Barnacles, ice nubbins, jellisacs, dirt piles, peat bogs, paper trees, fireflies, salmon, sloths, and dust traps fill the streets the archive says they lived on.

cards.title: Plant a tree
cards.text: Tend a Patch, plant a seasoned bean, pet the seedling, and watch a living tree take its place on the street.

cards.title: Foxes and Heli Kitties
cards.text: Fox preserves have their Rangers, licenses, bait, and brushable foxes; Heli Kitties hover, startle, and purr on 33 streets.

cards.title: Meditate and teleport
cards.text: The Focusing Orb meditates, focuses, and levitates; teleport points and one-way Teleportation Scripts join the map.

cards.title: Seven races and Game of Crowns
cards.text: Ticket Dispensers start Space Race, Crystal Climb, The Amazing Race, Time Warp, Canyon Run, Lava Leap, and Star Sprint, rebuilt from their recordings.

cards.title: Make a house a home
cards.text: Decorate with 43 pieces of recovered furniture, choose wallpaper and floors, and cultivate gardens, trees, and rocks on your home street.

cards.title: The whole skill tree
cards.text: All 105 skills are browsable; ranks now change mining, refining, gardening, and cooking, and starter skills bring their prerequisites.

cards.title: Neighbours and notes
cards.text: Street mailboxes open your mail anywhere, notes and notice boards carry new Glitch-voiced writing, and Visiting Stones lead to six neighbours' homes.

cards.title: The Rooks return
cards.text: A Forehorseman heralds the attack; stun the Rook with your Focusing Orb and shrine, then revive rooked critters and trees with balm.

cards.title: Friends stay grounded
cards.text: Local companions no longer climb into the canopy, and the stand-in Glitches are now off unless you ask for them.

posts.label: CATALOGUE SCALE
posts.title: Eesti Page 17 put the furniture back
posts.summary: The tiny quest now crosses the recording’s white sofa, sleepy cat, lamp, ornate chair, curled table, and cake in the right order.
posts.eyebrow: RECOVERED K04 ROOM · SOURCE DIALOGUE · ORIGINAL MUSIC
posts.subtitle: A very big little room feels like itself again.
posts.lead: The catalogue room had been mirrored and built from the wrong sofa, chair, and table variants. It now follows the supplied run from left to right with the exact clean K04 furniture, three framed cats, tabletop ornaments, and the cake hiding its shiny secret. Mr. Hairball animates while speaking, the two quest conversations retain their real boundary and wording, and reaching the hiding spot creates the item through collision like the source location. The recovered Eesti soundtrack replaces generic ambient music; no recording pixels or audio were used.

stat.caption: the recovered production instance’s original entry x-coordinate

cards.title: The correct curled table
cards.text: k04_table_03 restores the recording’s long twin-curled silhouette in place of the unrelated pedestal table.

cards.title: A physical search path
cards.text: Sofa, chair, and table platforms form the miniature climb, while contact behind the cake now discovers the object automatically.

cards.title: Eesti has its own music
cards.text: The clean recovered eesti_life_catalogue track is now the dedicated ambience for production hub 49.

posts.label: RED TAPE
posts.title: Legalize It took the long way around
posts.summary: The recorded subway round trip, forest briefing, Hall wait, and single clerk handoff now form one source-correct route.
posts.eyebrow: SEVEN SCENES · RECOVERED CLERKS · EXACT QUESTION
posts.subtitle: A qualification should require a little travel.
posts.lead: The quest no longer jumps from an invented Back Alley platform directly into the Hall. It now travels from Gregarious Grange Subway Station into the forest, hears all four Shady Bureaucrat beats, rides back through the station, crosses Gregarious Grange, waits ten seconds in the Hall, and survives one recorded clerk transfer before the Beige-or-Other question. Clean recovered art and animation sheets replace placeholders; recording blur and compression remain outside the game.

stat.caption: currants, cash only, followed by a separate pack activation

cards.title: The whole round trip
cards.text: Two subway platforms, the Back Alley forest, Gregarious Grange, and the Hall each keep their own clean composition and camera context.

cards.title: Please wait
cards.text: Walking into the waiting area now begins the source ten-second delay before the first named clerk calls Ur forward.

cards.title: Beige or Other
cards.text: The recorded final question and one handoff replace the invented multi-clerk loop, while purchase and activation remain separate actions.

posts.label: BLUE-SKY MEMORY
posts.title: A Summer’s Day remembered its true colors
posts.summary: The owl’s four recorded challenges now lead through bright white silhouettes to eight pale Annex dots and the recovered hanging ladder.
posts.eyebrow: SOURCE DIALOGUE · RECOVERED PULSE DOTS · CLEAN ART
posts.subtitle: The Annex is blue, white, and worth the climb.
posts.lead: The memory now keeps its authored pale-blue light instead of inheriting Dametime tint. A small white owl delivers all four source-observed prompts beside clean white platform and pillar silhouettes, while the Annex restores eight pale pulse dots worth exactly 8 iMG apiece and the original hanging-ladder exit. Every visual is clean recovered or native vector art—no recording pixels or compression artifacts were carried over.

stat.caption: optional Annex iMG when all eight pale memory dots are gathered

cards.title: The owl speaks again
cards.text: “Hey, I’m up here!”, “Not bad.”, “Almost there.”, and “Wow, you’re pretty good!” restore the four recorded guide beats.

cards.title: Eight pale rewards
cards.text: Recovered pulseDot art replaces generic quoins; each optional pickup grants the source-exact +8 iMG.

cards.title: The way home hangs overhead
cards.text: The recovered Firebog ladder now descends from the Annex ceiling in place of the invented rounded door.

posts.label: FIRST SNOW
posts.title: Winter Walk found its way home
posts.summary: The five-minute journey now climbs through Winter Haven, returns to the surface, and ends in the recording’s final white light.
posts.subtitle: The missing third act is back.
posts.lead: Winter Haven no longer sends the player straight home through a duplicate generic portal. Its recovered wooden ladder and EXIT sign lead back into Winter Walk, where three source-valued motes—1,098, 600, and 720 iMG—cross the last snowy platforms to a clean white home light.

stat.caption: winter motes across surface, Haven, and homeward finale

cards.title: Snow to stone
cards.text: The wide surface traverse still descends into the vertical Haven within the original five-minute clock.

cards.title: A real exit
cards.text: Recovered clean ladder and EXIT-sign art replace the invented glowing doorway at the top of Winter Haven.

cards.title: Homeward light
cards.text: The recorded return load, exact final reward trio, and bright surface exit now complete the route before Ur resumes.

posts.label: NEAR DAWN
posts.title: Starlit Night learned how to light up
posts.summary: Twenty source stars now bloom across the recovered night field before the plain moon gives way to its original smile.
posts.eyebrow: RECOVERED EVENT GRAPH · ORIGINAL VECTOR STATES
posts.subtitle: The reward is the sky changing around you.
posts.lead: The generic star field, drawn moon, and invented gold wash are gone. Eight clean source star panels fill the location, each revealed star uses its original artwork and one-second fade, and the final quoin now waits for the production 1.5-second moon transformation before opening the way home.

stat.caption: reward quoins driving 20 star reveals and one smiling-moon finale

cards.title: The actual night field
cards.text: Eight recovered stars_2 panels restore the dense, softly layered sky from the source street.

cards.title: Stars with a cue
cards.text: Twenty hidden source stars now fade into their exact coordinates as the corresponding rewards are gathered.

cards.title: A moon-sized payoff
cards.text: The original plain and smiling SWFs now perform the recovered 1.5-second final reveal before the exit unlocks.

posts.label: DEEP NIGHT
posts.title: Radial Heights found its moon again
posts.summary: The 53-star spiral now curls past the enormous smiling moon that defines the source course’s finale.
posts.eyebrow: ORIGINAL VECTOR ART · SOURCE STREET COORDINATES
posts.subtitle: A proper landmark among the stars.
posts.lead: The empty lower spiral now carries the recovered CC0 moon at its exact production position and 322-pixel size. Its original SWF was exported directly to scalable vector art, so the friendly face stays crisp without borrowing blur or compression from the gameplay recording.

stat.caption: source-authored stars orbiting one restored smiling moon

cards.title: The missing finale
cards.text: The giant moon now anchors the lower spiral exactly where the original street placed it.

cards.title: One coordinate system
cards.text: Moon and collectibles share the recovered GHFQOLEIHN63P27 screen-space layout.

cards.title: Crisp at course scale
cards.text: The original SWF is rasterized from vector paths at 322×322 instead of stretching a thumbnail.

posts.label: LATER
posts.title: Slip ’N Slide found its winter landmarks
posts.summary: The snowy run now passes the same friendly snowman, log cabins, ice spires, tree copses, and way-home castle seen in the source.
posts.subtitle: A hill is better when you know where you are.
posts.lead: The momentum course keeps its smooth authored collision hills, but generic triangle trees and an inferred finish shape are gone. Clean original K03 artwork now makes each stretch recognizable while preserving every star, jump, slope, and reward.

stat.caption: preloaded recovered scenery pieces with no mid-run pop-in

cards.title: A familiar welcome
cards.text: The exact smiling K03 snowman and first log cabin now establish the opening hill.

cards.title: Readable hill rhythm
cards.text: Two ice spires, two cabins, two snowy copses, and 24 archived trees give the long course distinct beats.

cards.title: The castle way home
cards.text: The recovered snow castle now frames the final stars and exit, matching the recorded destination.

posts.label: AFTER MIDNIGHT
posts.title: Cloud Rings finally fills the sky
posts.summary: Five clean, full-height cloud tunnels replace the small blurry hoops that used to interrupt Paradise.
posts.subtitle: Fly through a wall of weather.
posts.lead: The source course frames each ring as an enormous colored cloud mass that continues beyond the top and bottom of the location view. The remake now builds that same silhouette from crisp procedural lobes, with a generous readable opening and none of the blur caused by enlarging tiny cloud thumbnails.

stat.caption: animated vector cloud lobes across five towering rings

cards.title: Viewport-scale tunnels
cards.text: Each colored ring now reaches beyond the visible sky, matching the imposing foreground framing of the recorded course.

cards.title: Crisp at every scale
cards.text: Layered vector bodies, shadows, and highlights replace visibly stretched low-resolution puffs.

cards.title: Still fair to fly
cards.text: Larger collision openings preserve smooth traversal while all five rings, rewards, and the way home complete normally.

posts.label: LATE NIGHT
posts.title: The Faded Heart gets its full goodbye
posts.summary: The Phantom now finishes materializing and giving its Heart before any reward screen interrupts the street.
posts.subtitle: First the apparition. Then the reward.
posts.lead: Ordinary echoes now emerge through the complete clean 54-frame sequence instead of snapping into place. The final Phantom plays all 89 recovered heart-handoff frames, holds the revealed Heart for a breath, and only then yields to the original four-page quest completion.

stat.caption: clean handoff frames preserved from first shimmer to final Heart

cards.title: Echoes materialize
cards.text: Each haunting becomes readable during its source animation, remains clickable, and settles into the final silhouette.

cards.title: A complete handoff
cards.text: The 4.635-second recovered sheet and 700-millisecond Heart reveal now play without an early fade.

cards.title: Awards wait their turn
cards.text: Quest pages appear after the scene, with any earned level-up still queued safely behind them.

posts.label: NIGHT
posts.title: Rooks’ Woods grew crooked again
posts.summary: A layered bare-forest silhouette now makes every rise, root, and stretch of solid ground easier to read.
posts.subtitle: The path belongs to the forest.
posts.lead: The alpha run’s defining low canopy and enormous crooked limbs return through recovered CC0 tree, branch, and root art. Four deterministic depth layers bind the authored collision path into the scenery while keeping the avatar and ground edge distinct.

stat.caption: forest depths composed without a single recording pixel

cards.title: Thirty-one clean decos
cards.text: Thin distance trees, broken midground trunks, hanging canopy roots, and broad foreground bases come from the recovered art archive.

cards.title: Crooked by design
cards.text: Five authored limbs restore the hunched woodland rhythm visible in the reference without copying its dark, compressed pixels.

cards.title: Ground stays legible
cards.text: The original playable platform map is unchanged; roots now visually explain its rises while the top edge remains a continuous navigation cue.

posts.label: AFTER MIDNIGHT
posts.title: The Last Feat found its Glitch train
posts.summary: Local Glitches can now be followed from street to street, just as the recording shows.
posts.subtitle: Pick a Glitch. Fall into step.
posts.lead: The Last Feat is not only a three-line Incantation. Its players form a moving group first. Amp, Bumbishfish, and Lily Linguistic are now interactable world players: choose Follow and the avatar smoothly trails that Glitch until manual movement takes over or Stop following is selected.

stat.caption: distinct streets followed for the original non-creepy designation

cards.title: A real follow verb
cards.text: Companions use the same hover, click, and verb-menu language as every other street actor.

cards.title: The group carries on
cards.text: The selected name and trailing assist survive ordinary street loads while direct movement remains in the player’s hands.

cards.title: Source badge restored
cards.text: Three unique streets grant Stalker, Non-Creepy Designation with its original 200 iMG and 25 Friendly favor.

posts.label: MIDNIGHT
posts.title: The Stoot memorial has room to breathe
posts.summary: The private shrine no longer fills itself with unrelated street ecology.
posts.subtitle: One strange monument. Nothing in the way.
posts.lead: The archived unnnn location contains no ordinary item population, exactly as the supplied memorial recording shows. It now stays free of fallback trants, rocks, vendors, shrines, animals, quoins, and local companions, while the clean authored memorial and its pull-string doll load on every visit.

stat.caption: unrelated ecology actors left in the private memorial

cards.title: Empty by source
cards.text: A new explicit ecology row preserves the archived XML’s absence of location items instead of inventing fallback content.

cards.title: Always a memorial
cards.text: The monument now initializes whenever the recovered street loads, including saved and ordinary visits—not only its QA route.

cards.title: Recorded arrival
cards.text: The player arrives beside rather than inside the plaque, and the missing hub label is restored as Alphermia Prime.

posts.label: LATE NIGHT
posts.title: Cloud Rings became cloud tunnels
posts.summary: Five airy, color-shifting passages replace the old geometric hoops.
posts.subtitle: Fly through the clouds, not an outline.
posts.lead: The supplied Cloud Rings recording establishes enormous, soft vertical tunnels in yellow, orange, and purple. The remake now builds all five from clean local CC0 cloud puffs, preserving the navigable openings and course collision logic without copying a single recorded pixel.

stat.caption: primary animated cloud puffs, plus clean depth shadows

cards.title: Soft source artwork
cards.text: Two recovered fluffy-cloud assets form varied, overlapping silhouettes instead of thin vector ellipses.

cards.title: Openings preserved
cards.text: Each color profile keeps a deliberate inner flight corridor, so the new volume never changes the five-ring objective.

cards.title: Course verified
cards.text: Deterministic flight still collects all five rings and unlocks the exit; the full regression suite remains green.

posts.label: NIGHT
posts.title: Every quest gets the last word
posts.summary: Source-authored completion conversations now finish before transient rooms let go.
posts.subtitle: The reward can wait for the punchline.
posts.lead: Four Letter Words and Ilmenskie Jones confirmed that the Faded Heart panel was not a one-off. Every catalog quest now reads its original completion pages and player responses, keeps rewards for the final page, and waits for OK or close before leaving a temporary quest room.

stat.caption: catalog quests with recovered multi-page completion writing

cards.title: Original client art
cards.text: The recovered quest book now anchors the dark live-world panel, alongside its source-style close control.

cards.title: Authored cadence
cards.text: Every <split butt_txt> response becomes a real player-paced page instead of flattened prose.

cards.title: Reward pills restored
cards.text: iMG, currants, mood, energy, favor, and items receive readable source-colored pills on the final page only.

posts.label: LATER
posts.title: The Phantom found time to speak—twice
posts.summary: The handoff and its quiet four-page epilogue now follow the original recording.
posts.subtitle: Listen first. Remember after.
posts.lead: The supplied finale recording shows four player-paced exchanges before the Phantom hands over the Faded Heart, followed by four more Quest Complete pages. The remake now preserves both halves, triggers the clean handoff animation and reward exactly once, and waits for every original response.

stat.caption: recorded dialogue beats before and after the heart changes hands

cards.title: The street stays alive
cards.text: The completion view is a compact dark panel over the live world, not a full-screen celebration that hides the scene.

cards.title: Every response restored
cards.text: “I dunno.”, “Yeah…”, and “Do you think?” advance the exact source-authored lines before the final OK.

cards.title: Rewards wait their turn
cards.text: iMG, energy, and mood remain hidden until the final remembrance page, matching the recorded reward reveal.

posts.label: LATE
posts.title: The ground came back into view
posts.summary: One source-backed camera rule now frames homes, authored rooms, and every imported street.
posts.subtitle: Feet, ground, then pack.
posts.lead: The home reported a 540px world with its ground at y=620. Other scenes mixed raw art bounds, collision bounds, and hand-set camera starts. The camera now derives its usable world height from the deepest walkable ground instead.

stat.caption: internal pixels of consistent ground clearance above the pack

cards.title: Original vertical anchor
cards.text: The released client’s center plus scaled 150/600 y-offset resolves to a 75% avatar anchor, now shared by ordinary streets and homes.

cards.title: Authored rooms repaired
cards.text: Home exterior, interior, and other constructed scenes no longer trust a declared height that ends above their collision ground.

cards.title: Catalog-wide regression
cards.text: Automated coverage checks the lowest platform across more than 1,400 imported streets, plus the exact malformed-home case.

posts.title: The night the world woke up
posts.summary: Stories, races, flight courses, world systems, and a generous pile of polish.

cards.title: The clean-art promise
cards.text: The gameplay recordings are behavioral references. Visuals come from CC0 location data, original atlases, recovered SWFs, or crisp authored replacements.
items: No video blur copied into the game.
No compression seams treated as geometry.
No broken alpha frames promoted as assets.

blocks.label: Clickable milestones from the July 21 to 22 build

items.title: Actions gained a pulse
items.text: Physical verbs became timed and cancellable. Crafting gained per-item progress, partial completion, tool animation, and honest reward timing.

items.title: The pack became a place
items.text: Items could be used, sold, dropped, merged, collected, and restored after reload. Versioned saves came to cover the wider world state.

items.title: Residents found their routines
items.text: Piggies, Chickens, Butterflies, and six trant species gained rank-aware care, feeding, harvests, daily limits, dialogue, and persistent state.

items.title: Every street found its cast
items.text: Official archived location data supplied 1,084 street rows of animals, trees, rocks, gardens, vendors, Giant shrines, and confirmed empty private locations, placed with one collision-aware planner.

cards.title: Systems that joined the loop
items: Official XP levels, skill study, Dametime, food memory, buffs, tool wear, and repair.
Street Spirit vendors, four catalogs, drag-to-sell, drop piles, Giant donations, and eight quoin types.
Musicblocks, Triple Jump, camera polish, speech bubbles, Wood Trees, living trants, and Animal Kinship.
Exact achievement counters and three recovered gameplay-video badges.

cards.title: What live QA proved
items: Completed actions rewarded; cancelled actions did not.
Animal care, quest progress, inventory, favors, and tool condition survived reloads.
Fresh games started muted and browser logs finished clean.
